method: logit marginal effects for binary outcomes
layout: outcomes as columns, each outcome twice: pooled project (odd columns) and separate arms (even columns)
tags.picture_matters: The text layer interleaves the columns: Project and arm estimates from different columns land on the same text line (e.g. '0.263*** (0.0335)' mixes column 1's estimate with column 2's SE), so which arm and which outcome each number belongs to must be read from the picture.

Notes: ... The specifications include standard control variables from the baseline survey ... (see Table 4 ...). We have applied the logit model for binary outcome variables and show the marginal effects. Standard errors are clustered at the district cluster level.
context_needed: Burchi and Strupat (DIE), Tingathe Economic Empowerment Pilot (EEP), Malawi: a cluster-randomised trial among Social Cash Transfer beneficiary households with three components (lump-sum plus training, lump-sum only, training only) against control (PDF page 22). 'Project' is the pooled effect of any component (equation 1); the three arm rows come from a separate regression with one dummy per component (equation 2). Assignment is by cluster, so these are intent-to-treat estimates. Round: the single follow-up survey, June-July 2017 (PDF page 22). The table note says binary outcomes are logit marginal effects; the amount columns are linear regressions (Section 3, PDF page 24: logit or Poisson only for binary or count outcomes). Units: probability (yes/no columns) and Malawian kwacha.

not_stored.reason: covariate coefficients; estimated but not printed. If a table printed their marginal effects they would not be stored either

not_stored.cell: Blank cells (e.g. column 1 for the arm rows, column 2 for Project)
not_stored.reason: no estimate: each outcome is run once pooled and once by arm, in different columns

rule: In a logit or probit of an outcome on treatment, the printed marginal effect of the treatment dummy is the programme effect: store it as a change in probability with specification naming the model, and never store covariate coefficients or marginal effects. A probit of treatment or of attrition on baseline characteristics (a participation, balance or attrition model) is not an outcome model and gives no stored rows.
